text.p: Following is the full text of a statement by Belgian group POWERFIN .
Press release
CONTINUED INVESTMENT STABILISED PROFITS INCREASED DIVIDEND
PROPOSED MERGER WITH TRACTEBEL - 3 POWERFIN SHARES FOR 1 TRACTEBEL SHARE

POWERFIN, which undertakes most of the investments in the electricity and gas industries made outside Belgium by TRACTEBEL, the Belgian industrial services and public utilities multinational, today announced a proposed merger with its parent company, TRACTEBEL S.A. The merger will give POWERFIN additional financial resources and raise its profile internationally. It will also give it the industrial backing it needs to qualify for certain projects.

The merger proposal will be submitted to the AGMs of the respective companies, and the actual operation will be effected by an exchange of one new TRACTEBEL share for every three POWERFIN shares. The fairness of the exchange, both for TRACTEBEL shareholders and for POWERFIN shareholders, and from the financial point of view, has been confirmed without reservation by SBC WARBURG and by KREDIETBANK SECURITIES and PETERCAM SECURITIES in their capacity as investment banks.
POWERFIN continued its strategy of investment in 1996. Its net consolidated profits have remained stable at BEF 7.7 billion.

POWERFIN' s shareholders will largely recover their growth potential in TRACTEBEL; besides the important presence of ELECTRABEL in both companies, TRACTEBEL owns more than 60% of POWERFIN and 100% of GROUPE FABRICOM, whose operational sectors are already showing growth.
Results summary
Table omitted.
In 1996, POWERFIN continued its strategy of investment abroad, with the acquisition or development of ten new projects in Chile, Thailand, Singapore, Canada, the USA, Kazakhstan and China.
The contribution made by the operating companies abroad to the consolidated results has risen, mainly because CRSS was consolidated for 12 months in 1996, as opposed to only six in 1995.
The stabilisation of the consolidated profits has been accompanied by an increase in the costs of financing and developing projects abroad.
Commenting on the forthcoming merger with TRACTEBEL, Mr. Daniel Deroux, director of POWERFIN and head of the TRACTEBEL group's Electricity and Gas International business unit, stated:

The merger of POWERFIN with TRACTEBEL is a necessary operation, since it will give us enhanced credibility in international markets. Thanks to its activities in Belgium, and to the numerous achievements of TRACTEBEL ENGINEERING outside Belgium, TRACTEBEL S.A. is able to provide the industrial backing which POWERFIN often lacks.

In the field, our negotiators currently are only credible if they produce TRACTEBEL business cards. The coexistence of TRACTEBEL with POWERFIN as a financial vehicle of our projects is often confusing for the people we have to deal with. From this point of view, the merger with TRACTEBEL represents an important step in carrying our strategy forward.
More detailed information is attached.

2. Investments
In 1996 POWERFIN invested BEF 18.8 billion. This amount includes investments by the companies consolidated fully, proportionally, or by the equity method. 3. Sector results
TAble omitted
The growth of POWERFIN's share in the net consolidated profits of ELECTRABEL reflects the increase in the latter company's profits.
The improved contribution from operating companies abroad is mainly due to:
- the greater contribution by CRSS in the USA, which was acquired in June 1995 and so only contributed to the results for six months of that year;
- the coming on-stream of the MANAH power station in Oman.
- The growth in the other elements of the results reflects the rise in the costs of financing and developing projects abroad.

Amortisation of consolidation goodwill came to BEF 330 million, compared with BEF 137 million in 1995. This increase is a direct consequence of the acquisitions carried out in 1996, together with the consolidation of CRSS over a period of 12 months instead of 6 as in 1995. It is also a logical consequence of the accounting principles applied by POWERFIN for amortisation of goodwill, which are much more conservative than those used by some foreign groups active in the same sector.
Since the beginning of 1996, the group has acquired or developed ten new electricity or gas projects in Chile, Thailand, Singapore, Canada, the USA, Kazakhstan and China.
Construction work was completed in Oman, and is continuing in Italy, Chile, India, Thailand and China, according to schedule.
North America

In June 1996, under the terms of a preliminary agreement, the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) awarded development of a 400 MW lignite-fired fluidised bed power station jointly to CRSS and Phillips Coal (a member of the Philips Petroleum group). In October 1996, CRSS announced the acquisition of two cogeneration plants in the USA, Nepco (50 MW) and Ripon (47 MW), and the purchase of a 30% stake in a third, Iroquois Falls (110 MW) in Canada.

CRSS operates 15 power stations in the USA and Canada, and is developing a 16th, giving it a total capacity of 1,287 MW. The plants concerned are mostly cogeneration stations which burn biomass or recycled fuel. The load factor and efficiency of the CRSS generating units are kept at a very high level everywhere.
South America

In Argentina, the TRACTEBEL group is responsible for distributing 2.5 billion mx of gas per year in Santa Fe province and the north-west of Buenos Aires province. LITORAL GAS, the company which carries out this activity, closed this financial year, like previous ones, with a profit.

In Chile, the group acquired control of the Tocopilla coal-fired power station (594 MW), in March 1996, and made major efforts into increase performance by bringing the organisation up to speed and improving the supply of fuel. Since October 1996, POWERFIN has controlled the entire Colbn-Machicura power complex, comprising three hydro-electric power stations already in service (523 MW) and two under construction (520 MW), with commissioning scheduled for 1998.
Asia

In 1996, the State of Kazakhstan sold generating installations to POWERFIN representing a capacity of 1,307 MW of electricity and 875 MWeq of heat, along with power transmission and distribution networks serving the towns in Almaty province.
As was to be expected, the takeover of these operations was not without problems, but the necessary measures were taken to rectify situation before the onset of winter 1996/1997.

In the Sultanate of Oman, the 100 MW d'Al Manah power station built by the TRACTEBEL group was commissioned ahead of schedule. The company also began construction of a 27 MW fluidised bed generating plant at Zhenjiang in China, and is continuing the task of setting up a natural gas transportation network with a capacity of 1.2 billion mx per year in the greater Bangkok region of Thailand.

In Singapore the group won the tender for development of a power and services complex on the artificial island of Pulan Sakra, including a cogeneration station with a capacity of 365 MW of electricity and 95 MWeq of heat.
Finally, the group is building a 260 MW power plant in India.
Europe

The load factor of the Kilroot and Belfast West power stations (900 MW) in Northern Ireland was maintained at a high level. In Italy, the 352 MW cogeneration plant built by POWERFIN in Rosignano is due to come on stream in the second half of 1997.

In December 1995, POWERFIN acquired control of the Dunamenti power station in Hungary. At the end of 1996, POWERFIN was forced to conclude that the conditions for remuneration for the services provided by the Dunamenti power station were considerably out of line with those that were offered by the Hungarian government at the time of the acquisition. POWERFIN has therefore commenced legal proceedings to rescind the sale, leading to a process of consultation which is now underway.
POWERFIN also has minority stakes in eight power stations (25 MW) in Portugal, and in the City of Bremen public services authority (1,210 MW). 4 TRACTEBEL-POWERFIN merger
The boards of TRACTEBEL and POWERFIN have announced their agreement on the terms of a proposed merger between the two companies, with retrospective effect from 1 January 1997.

5. Company results and dividend
The net non-consolidated profit made by POWERFIN S.A. came to BEF 6,363 million in 1996, compared with BEF 6,634 million in 1995, a fall of BEF 271 million.
At the AGM on 21 May 1997, the board of directors will propose in increase in the net unit dividend to BEF 121 per share for financial year 1996, compared with BEF 115 for 1995.
In the case of shares accompanied by a VVPR strip giving entitlement to a reduced rate of withholding tax, the dividend will be to BEF 137.13, compared with BEF 130.33 the previous year.
These dividends will be payable as of 28 May 1997, on presentation of No.8.coupons.
Note that POWERFIN stripped its VVPR shares on May 9, converting each VVPR share into an ordinary share accompanied by a VVPR strip.
